why: Made-up routes test the shared serializer for the storage refusals. Their real doors are met in tests/storage-inventory.test.ts (the installation totals), tests/storage-destinations.test.ts (the destination doors' refusals for an unpermitted caller, invalid fields, an unsafe host secrets file, and one code for every check of the file), tests/storage-destinations-in-an-installed-office.test.ts (an installed bundle with no sandbox templates, where each check is refused through the real doors) and tests/storage-restore-media.test.ts (an attachment left out of a restored backup). Those tests make the host secrets file and the omissions journal they need. No door here has them.

refusals.english: Test: only the person or a secretary may read these totals.
Test: the destination fields are invalid.
Test: this caller may not change storage destinations.
Test: the host secrets file cannot be used safely.
Test: more than one sandbox template names a secrets file.
Test: a folder above the secrets file is a link.
Test: no folder above the secrets file exists.
Test: the secrets file is not a plain file with one name.
Test: other users may read the secrets file.
Test: the secrets file belongs to another user.
Test: the secrets file is larger than 1 MiB.
Test: the secrets file changed while it was read.
Test: the office could not read the secrets file.
Test: the office could not write the secrets file.
Test: this attachment was left out of the backup.
